 Soccer-Healthy again, Kompany wants to shift focus back to football normality
 Thursday, 19 Nov 2026
 | 6:31 PM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 FILE PHOTO: Soccer Football - UEFA Champions League - Bayern Munich v Arsenal - Allianz Arena, Munich, Germany - October 21, 2026 Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany reacts. REUTERS/Angelika Warmuth/File Photo 
 MUNICH, Germany, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Bayern ⁠Munich coach Vincent Kompany is thankful for the support he ⁠received after falling ill and collapsing but said on Thursday he ‌was eager to go back to football normality, with the focus on results.
 Kompany returns to the bench on Friday after almost a month out.The Belgian coach had been rushed to ​hospital on October 23 after collapsing during a ⁠second-team training session, having nursed ⁠a virus in the days before.
 He was diagnosed with ameningeal irritation and was ⁠discharged ‌from hospitala few days later.
 "I am thankful for the support," Kompany told a press conference, sporting a strapped shoulder after surgery unrelated ⁠to the virus. "I had immediate support from the club ​and the doctors. ‌You try not to think about what could have happened."
 Kompany, speaking before ⁠Bayern host ​Cologne in the league onFriday, said he had undergone scores of tests and was healthy.
 "I feel good. I had a long process ... and now is the time for ⁠the next step. I would just like for ​everything to go back to normal as quickly as possible," he said.
 Kompany, in his third season at Bayern, said it was interesting to see the team ⁠from a different perspective, especially their 2-0 win at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.
 Bayern won four and drew one of their five matches under assistant coach Aaron Danks.
 The Bavarians are in top spot in the Bundesliga, ahead ​of Borussia Dortmund on goal difference, and are ⁠unbeaten in four matches in the Champions League.
 "I am here, what happened has ​happened and it can happen to anyone," ‌Kompany said. "From tomorrow, it will be back ​to normal about games lost and games won and hopefully this will be the priority."
 (Reporting by Karolos Grohmann; Editing by Kevin Liffey)
